item.title: South Africa claim Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry trophy as All Blacks fall short in final Test
item.description: The Rugby's Greatest Rivalry tour has ended in heartbreak, with South Africa defeating the All Blacks 43-28 in a nail-biting fourth test. The Springboks lead the All Blacks 17-14 at halftime in Baltimore.
item.content:encoded:
The Rugby's Greatest Rivalry tour has ended in heartbreak, with South Africa defeating the All Blacks 43-28 in a nail-biting fourth test.

The Springboks lead the All Blacks 17-14 at halftime in Baltimore.

They dominated for much of the first half, but the All Blacks struck back with four minutes left when Will Jordan surged over for a try, to go with one from Codie Taylor early in the game.

There was a lengthy delay midway through the first half, when referee Karl Dickson lost communication with the Television Match Official.

Play resumed after the two captains agreed that there would not be TMO involvement unless there was foul play, in which case a phone call would be made.

British Open golf winner Ryan Fox carred the New Zealand flag, standing next to the All Blacks at the pre-match anthem.

The All Blacks won the first Test 33-16, with the Springboks taking the next three games 33-26, 29-24 and now 43-28.

item.title: Dolphins down Warriors 26-16 to reach preliminary finals
item.description: The Dolphins are through to the NRL preliminary finals after defeating the Warriors 26-16 last night. The Dolphins ran in four tries to one to etch their name in the history books.
item.content:encoded:
The Dolphins are through to the NRL preliminary finals after defeating the Warriors 26-16 last night.

The Dolphins ran in four tries to one to etch their name in the history books.

Selwyn Cobbo, Herbie Farnworth, Hamiso Tabuai-Fidow and Jack Bostock scored a try apiece for the Queensland side.

Meanwhile, the Warriors have another chance to qualify for the preliminary finals, as they will face the Newcastle Knights next weekend.

In another result last night, the Sharks beat the Cowboys 26-16.

The Sharks will take on the loser of the Panthers and Roosters match.

Coming up today, the Panthers will meet the Roosters at 6.05pm.

item.title: Flying Fijians defeat Canada 45-29, move closer to PNC title defence
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 13/09/2026 The FIJI Water Flying Fijians defeated Canada 45-29 in their Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup clash tonight, putting them in a strong position to defend their title.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 13/09/2026

The FIJI Water Flying Fijians defeated Canada 45-29 in their Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup clash tonight, putting them in a strong position to defend their title.

Fiji started strongly, with Kitione Salawa crossing the try line within the first minute to put Fiji 7-0 ahead.

They continued to apply pressure on the Canadians and starved them of possession.

Some great handling was on display from Fiji, as they managed to put Frank Lomani over the try line to extend their lead to 14-0.

Canada managed to score their first try through Mason Flesch, closing the gap to 14-7.

The Flying Fijians did not let up as they continued to push forward, determined to ensure the title returns to the islands.

Isaiah Armstrong-Ravula and Peni Ravai scored tries before halftime to give Fiji a 26-17 lead at the break.

Fiji started the second half strongly again, with captain Tevita Ikanivere scoring in the fifth minute, followed by a double from Motikiai Murray.

The Canadians did not quit, continuing to push for their third try, which came in the 65th minute when Kyle Tremblay crossed the try line.

The try was a boost for Canada as they matched Fiji’s physicality, with Flesch following through on a kick and managing to outmuscle Isikeli Rabitu to score their fourth try.

Fiji played the final minutes with 13 men after Isoa Nasilasila and Terio Tamani were shown yellow cards. However, Nasilasila’s yellow card was upgraded to a red following a TMO review.

Meanwhile, Japan thrashed the USA 63-14.

Fiji will now turn their focus to next Saturday, where they will face Japan in the final at 9.05pm.
